title: Rank-heterogeneous Preference Models for School Choice

problem.claim: School choice mechanism designers need models to understand and predict families' preferences.

gap.claim: The widely used MNL model assumes that the choice process is uniform across all positions in ranked preference lists.

contributions.claim: A context-dependent random utility model adapts rank-heterogeneous choice modeling by treating down-rank choices as occurring in the context of earlier up-rank choices.
A rank-stratified choice model regularizes adjacent rank-specific models toward one another when appropriate.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On SFUSD household preference data from multiple years, contextual models considerably improve out-of-sample evaluation metrics across all rank positions compared with non-contextual models in the literature.
Rank-stratified modeling can produce more accurate first-choice predictions, while down-rank predictions are relatively unimproved.

narrative_sequence.summary: School choice researchers use discrete choice models to understand and predict family preferences.
MNL is simple and interpretable but assumes a uniform choice process throughout the ranking.
The paper introduces contextual and rank-stratified strategies for rank-heterogeneous modeling.
Contextual models improve reported out-of-sample metrics across rank positions, while rank stratification mainly improves first-choice predictions.
The models are presented as performance upgrades for school choice prediction and counterfactual analysis.

source_observation.claim: Modeling choices in the context of earlier ranked choices improves reported out-of-sample metrics across rank positions.

interpretation.claim: When preferences may vary by rank, conditioning on earlier choices can capture structure missed by a rank-uniform model.

application.claim: Consider context-dependent choice models for ranked-preference prediction and counterfactual analysis.

exception.claim: Rank-stratified modeling may improve first-choice predictions without materially improving down-rank predictions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the sample size or exact years of the SFUSD data.
The exact evaluation metrics, baseline implementations, and magnitude of improvements are not reported.
Model specifications, regularization choices, uncertainty estimates, and replication details are not provided.
